title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and that's a problem for America's space agency
gist: Eric Berger argues SpaceX has flipped from needing the US government to being indispensable to it, and is now retreating from new government spaceflight work (ending Dragon by 2030, no Falcon 9 commercial sales after 2028, declining Space Force bids and lunar lander launches) to focus on AI and Starlink/Starmind post-IPO. That leaves NASA's Artemis HLS and Moon Base plans exposed, with Blue Origin's New Glenn emerging as NASA's essential, but unproven, alternative.
